newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Osem value lowered.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Osem value lowered.

text.p: Bank Hapoalim lowered its valuation of Osem Investment to between $425 million and $465 million from between $490 million and $530 million, the bank said in a report on Wednesday.
The previous valuation was by the bank in August 1996.
Despite the lower valuation the bank reiterated its "hold" recommendation for the Israeli food company.

The new valuation is based on estimates that the financial results of the company will not "improve significantly" because of tough competition in the Israeli food industry and because of the high level of investment required to introduce new products into the market.
Hapoalim estimated net profit for 1997 at 70.5 million shekels against 74.9 million in 1996. Net profit in 1998 is estimated at 76.6 million shekels.
Earnings per share (EPS) for 1997 is estimated at 0.89 shekels, against an EPS of 0.92 in 1996. EPS for 1998 is estimated at 0.96 shekels.
"The main growth in sales in 1997 is expected to come in the ice-cream sector," the report said.
In 1996 Osem entered the ice-cream sector through a partnership with Tnuva, Israel's biggest food cooperative. The jointly produced ice-creams will be marketed in the coming summer months.
In 1996 Swiss food giant Nestle became the controlling shareholder in Osem, buying 40 percent of the company.
"In most of the activities of the company we expect a lower growth rate due mainly to the (slower) population growth," the report said.
